newsitem.title: UK: Analyst sees further shake-out for global tyremakers.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees further shake-out for global tyremakers.

text.p: The world's billion-dollar tyre industry, now dominated by three big players, could face a further shake-out, an industry analyst said on Thursday.
An international gathering of rubber growers, traders and tyre executives was also told that the future demand growth for tyres would come from Asia, excluding Japan, and Latin America.
Neil Mullineux, an auto industry expert and consultant at UK-based Bowfell Research Associates, said today's Big Three were Bridgestone, Michelin and Goodyear.
He said that 20 years ago there were 10 bigt tyre companies.
Since then, Firestone had been taken over by Bridgestone, Dunlop was purchased by Sumitomo, Uniroyal first merged with Goodrich and then the combined firm was taken over by French group Michelin.
"The very big companies will grow and will become stronger," Mullineux said. "They will have a global presence selling branded tyres at relatively high margins."
"Some of the smaller companies will also grow, making tyres cheaply," he said. But Mullineux said middle-sized firms risked being squeezed between the big and the small firms.
Industry watchers said recent developments pointed towards the underlying trend in the tyre business.
In March, U.S. firm Cooper Tire and Rubber Co said it agreed to buy the UK's Avon Rubber Plc tyre operations for about $110 million.
Japan's Sumitomo Rubber Industries Ltd said in February that it and Goodyear had agreed to produce tyres for cars using each other's brand names within this year.
Goodyear will manufacture up to two million passenger and light truck tyres in North America for Sumitomo unit Dunlop Tire Corp and Sumitomo affiliate Ohtsu Tire and Rubber Co Ltd.
In Japan, Sumitomo also will make up to two million Goodyear tyres for sale in that country.
Analysts said the move could lead to a deeper relationships between the two tyre giants.
"There is a feeling that to effectively supply the automotive sector, you have to be big," said David Shaw, editor of industry magazine European Rubber Journal. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
